risks: Quarterly margin and EPS benefited materially from tariff refunds, so headline profitability includes a non-operating tailwind.

AI functionality may fail to become a durable differentiated engagement or monetization layer; the present source does not establish that causal bridge.
Temporary tariff refunds inflate headline margin/EPS comparability and can create confidence inflation if treated as recurring.
Competitive/substitution response to Siri AI cannot be adjudicated from the present issuer release.
Headline margin and EPS contain a quantified temporary tariff-refund tailwind and should not be treated as fully recurring operating improvement.
Tariff policy and reciprocal measures remain an operating and supply-chain uncertainty; the filing discusses these measures but does not establish a stable long-run tariff regime.

The $57.0B manufacturing purchase-obligation base creates substantial near-term committed procurement exposure; the filing does not by itself establish how flexibly those obligations can be resized under a demand or supply shock.

contradictions: Record EPS and margin include a meaningful temporary tariff-refund benefit.
Record EPS and margin coexist with a material temporary tariff-refund benefit; recurring profitability should therefore be evaluated net of that benefit.
Record headline profitability coexists with a material temporary tariff-refund benefit; this qualifies, rather than falsifies, the strong consolidated execution signal.

Very strong reported gross-margin performance coexists with tariff-related policy volatility and previously disclosed temporary tariff-refund benefits, so recurring margin quality requires Alpha normalization rather than headline extrapolation.

Apple describes diversified component sourcing and adequate liquidity while simultaneously carrying $57.0B of manufacturing purchase obligations, $56.2B due within 12 months; this is resilience capacity plus meaningful execution commitment rather than evidence of either pure flexibility or pure fragility.
